Done. Built and committed a complete JSON REST API.

## What was built

**Stack:** Node.js ESM using only built-ins — `node:http` for the server (no Express/framework) and `node:sqlite` for a persistent on-disk database (`data/app.db`). Node 24 in this sandbox has both.

**Files:**
- `src/db.js` — SQLite connection + schema (`users`, `sessions`, `notes`), WAL mode, foreign keys.
- `src/store.js` — data-access layer: scrypt password hashing with per-user salt + constant-time verify, session issuance, note CRUD.
- `src/server.js` — HTTP router, JSON body parsing, bearer-token auth, error mapping.
- `test/api.test.js` — end-to-end tests over real HTTP.

**Endpoints:**
| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/signup` | — | `201 {id, username}` |
| POST | `/login` | — | `200 {session}` |
| GET | `/me` | bearer | `200 {id, username}` |
| POST | `/notes` | bearer | `201 {id, title, body, createdAt}` |
| GET | `/notes` | bearer | `200 [...]` (own notes only) |

**Behavior details:**
- Listens on `PORT` (default 3000). `npm start` added.
- Sessions are opaque 256-bit tokens stored server-side, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Bad requests handled: `400` (missing/malformed fields, non-object/invalid JSON), `401` (bad creds or missing/invalid token), `409` (duplicate username), `404` (unknown route), `413` (oversized body).
- Multi-user isolation: users only see their own notes (verified in tests).

**Verification:** All 7 tests pass, including one that **restarts the server process against the same DB file** and confirms users and notes persist. `node --check` passes on all files. Committed as `ca2058f`.
